definition: A fan of laser beams wired as a MIDI controller: breaking a beam with a hand triggers a synthesizer note. Jean-Michel Jarre's 2017 shows used a 20 W one.
Deliberately sweeping laser beams through the crowd at controlled exposure levels.
The unit Guinness counts for its largest laser show record: each point where a beam leaves a device, with a beam split by diffraction counted once.
A gas laser used on large 1990s tours; Pink Floyd's 1994 US tour carried two 50 W systems.
Optically pumped semiconductor laser, a solid-state source used in touring projectors such as the 35 W units on Jean-Michel Jarre's 2017 shows.
A surface or unit placed to catch a laser beam at the end of its path.
The International Laser Display Association, the laser show trade body, founded at Lake Tahoe on August 16, 1986.
The laser display industry's annual prizes, with artistic categories such as Beams/Atmospherics, Graphics, Planetarium and Live Stage.
ILDA's award for technical achievement.

ILDA Accredited Professional Lasershow Company: an industry credential requiring documented shows, client references, a staff member who has passed a Laser Safety Officer course and a signed safety affirmation.
What a laser company charges per day of show, worked out from equipment write-off, overhead and margin.
Permission from the US FDA to sell or run laser show equipment above Class IIIa (5 mW visible).
The US regulatory category that covers laser light show projectors.
A numbered FDA guidance letter to the laser industry, such as Laser Notice 51 (projector makers and dealers) and Laser Notice 56 (IEC conformance).
An FDA instruction that lets border staff detain listed firms' products without examining them; Import Alert 95-04 covers laser pointers and light show projectors.
Diode-pumped solid-state laser, the default show laser source from about 2005 until direct diodes took over, by one maker's account.
A semiconductor laser that emits the wanted color itself, such as 445 nm blue and about 520 nm green.
A projector feature that lets the operator widen or narrow the beam during a show.
The person who performs or operates a laser show, often mixing pre-programmed cues with live control. Also called a laser artist.
The trained person responsible for a show's laser safety; required in some jurisdictions (Germany, Arizona) and not in others.
A system that cuts the beam if the scanning mirrors stop moving; listed by the UK HSE among standard controls for laser displays.
A notice to pilots; UK guidance says one should be filed for outdoor laser beams.
